key_insight: MedGame turns static medical case studies into interactive, story-driven learning games powered by large language models. Instead of isolated Q&A, it creates an end-to-end clinical decision journey that guides learners through realistic choices and consequences.
problem_solved: Most LLM-based medical education tools focus on short, localized interactions such as single-turn questions or feedback. This paper addresses the lack of structured, case-level learning experiences that teach clinical reasoning across an entire patient trajectory.
method: Uses a dual-engine architecture to generate and run medical storytelling games.
A Medical Narrative Designer converts case-grounded clinical information into an interactive narrative with decision points.
The system supports structured, executable gameplay so learners can make choices and progress through the case dynamically.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, MedGame shows how LLMs can be used beyond chat to build educational simulations with richer pedagogy and stronger user engagement. It highlights a general design pattern for turning domain cases into interactive, decision-centered learning systems.

paper_title: MedGame: Storytelling Gamification Empowered by Large Language Models for Medical Education
paper_authors: Qian Wu, Xinrong Zhou, Zizhan Ma, Kai Chen, Zheyao Gao
